title: tool/merge_arb.py silently no-ops because all 4 hardcoded source branches (r1-tracks2 etc.) no longer exist
rule: Nygard lens: silent failure on missing input
area: tool (ARB merge, one-off R1 fix-wave helper)
why: `git branch -a` confirms none of the 4 branches this script reads from still exist locally or on the remote — they were the ephemeral R1 fix-wave worktree branches, presumably merged and deleted. load_branch_arb() swallows a failing `git show <branch>:<path>` into an empty dict with no warning, so running this script today prints '<path>: no new keys' for both ARBs — which reads as 'already in sync' when the real reason is 'none of the source branches exist.' A future dev who reruns this expecting it to pick up some other branches' ARB changes gets silent, misleading success.
recommendation: Either delete this one-off script now that its job (the R1 merge) is done (git history preserves it), or make it fail loudly when a listed branch doesn't resolve via `git rev-parse --verify <branch>` before attempting `git show`.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script against a nonexistent branch either exits non-zero with a clear error, or the script (and its stale branch list) is removed.
